title: QCon San Francisco 2026: How to Kill the Code Review
summary:
Ankit Jain of Aviator told QCon San Francisco 2026 that line-by-line code review is already fading, since most review comments concern knowledge sharing rather than defects and over 75% of PRs merge without human review. He proposed six layers: argue, capture, codify, prove, debate, own. His team merges four times more PRs, with about 40% fewer reverts.

title: Safe, automated bug discovery and fixing with Prospero
summary:
Fuzz testing remains an effective tool for discovering software defects, more so than ever with AI agents driving, fixing bugs on the fly, clearing the way for deeper fuzzing, all unattended. My coding harness, Prospero, is particularly suited for this task via its unique deploy to container feature. With a bit of one-time prep work, you can run agents within a no-network Docker or Podman container with instructions to set up and run a fuzzing campaign on your repository. Any fallout from the agent or fuzzing campaign is safely trapped in the container, while bug fixes flow out freely. As far as I’m aware, Prospero is the only AI tooling with this capability.
